title: How Much Does It Cost to Build a Web App? Here Are Your Options
summary: How much does it cost to build a web app? See real price ranges by build path, app type, and region to make an informed decision.
body_markdown:
TL;DR


## Key takeaways


-


A custom web app can cost about $20,000 for a focused MVP to $400,000 or more for a complex enterprise platform.


-


Scope, technical complexity, integrations, security, and who builds the app have the biggest effect on price.


-


Hosting may start below $100 per month, but third-party services and annual maintenance add ongoing costs after launch.


-


No-code and AI app builders can reduce upfront costs, while agencies provide deeper customization, testing, and support.


-


Modelence helps founders build and launch full-stack apps with authentication, databases, deployment, monitoring, and code ownership included.


Ask AI about this post:


A professionally built web app can cost roughly $20,000 for a focused minimum viable product (MVP) to $400,000 or more for an enterprise platform, with large or compliance-heavy systems sometimes exceeding $500,000.


The biggest variable is scope and technical complexity: user roles, integrations, real-time features, security requirements, and expected scale all push the price higher.


This guide breaks down the cost of web application development by component, app type, development path, region, hosting, third-party services, and maintenance.


It also compares agency, freelance, no-code, AI-builder, and self-built approaches before walking through two complete year-one budgets for bootstrapped and funded founders.


## **Web App Development Costs at a Glance**


For a professionally developed custom web app, current build costs generally fall into these ranges:


**Complexity** **Build cost** **Timeline** **Example**


Simple $20,000–$50,000 2–4 months Internal tool with login, profiles, and basic create, read, update, and delete (CRUD)


Mid-complexity $80,000–$150,000+ 4–8 months Software-as-a-service (SaaS) dashboard with accounts, payments, and integrations


Complex $150,000–$300,000+ 6–12 months Marketplace with multiple roles, messaging, and real-time features


Enterprise $200,000–$400,000+ 12–24+ months Multi-tenant platform with compliance and internal-system integrations


These ranges synthesize current industry estimates, which commonly place focused MVPs around $20,000–$50,000, business-ready applications around $80,000–$150,000 or more, and enterprise platforms above $200,000.


Timelines rise from roughly two to four months for a focused MVP to a year or longer for integration-heavy enterprise systems.


These are build costs only. Hosting, payment processing, authentication, email, storage, maintenance, and future feature work add ongoing expenses after launch.


## **Factors That Drive a Web Application’s Cost**


The cost of web application development is not one number. It is a collection of line items that agencies and freelancers may package differently, which is why two quotes for the same idea can look far apart.


**Component** **Typical cost**


Discovery and user interface/user experience (UI/UX) design 15–30% of the project budget


Frontend and backend development 50–70% of the project budget


Infrastructure and hosting $5–$500+ per month initially


Third-party integrations $0–$5,000+ to implement, plus usage fees


Testing, deployment, and project management 15–30% combined


**Discovery and design** cover requirements, user flows, wireframes, prototypes, and visual design. A template-led project stays near the lower end, while custom research and usability testing require more time.


**Frontend and backend development** usually consume the largest share of the budget. Together, they commonly represent 50–70% of total project spending because they include the interface, application programming interfaces (APIs), database logic, authentication, permissions, and integrations.


**Infrastructure and hosting** may start at only a few dollars per month for a low-traffic app, but managed databases, backups, load balancing, and additional environments increase the bill. Current estimates place early infrastructure costs between roughly $5 and $500 per month.


**Third-party services** include payment providers, email delivery, maps, authentication, analytics, and storage. Some are free at low usage, while complex API integrations can add thousands of dollars in implementation costs.


**Testing, deployment, and project management** cover quality assurance (QA), security checks, release preparation, automation, and coordination. These costs are essential for turning working code into a stable production application.


Any part a founder handles personally may disappear from the initial quote, but it becomes an ongoing responsibility or recurring monthly expense. That is where web app budgets often quietly expand.


## **Costs Also Vary by the Type of Web App You Want to Build**


Generic ranges only go so far. The type of application sets the baseline for its user roles, workflows, integrations, security, and infrastructure.


**App type** **Traditional build cost**


Internal tool or simple SaaS $20,000–$80,000


Customer-facing SaaS dashboard $80,000–$200,000+


Marketplace or two-sided platform $80,000–$300,000+


Ecommerce web app $20,000–$180,000+


Social or community platform $80,000–$300,000+


**Internal tools and simple SaaS:** Stay near the lower end when they serve few users and need limited integrations. Approval flows and internal system connections raise costs.


**Customer-facing SaaS dashboards:** Cost more because they need secure accounts, billing, analytics, integrations, and scalable data handling.


**Marketplaces and community platforms:** Require multiple user roles, messaging, moderation, reviews, notifications, disputes, and often split payments.


**Ecommerce applications:** Range from simple catalogs and checkout flows to complex systems with subscriptions, loyalty, inventory, marketplaces, and enterprise resource planning (ERP) or point-of-sale (POS) integrations.


Real AI functionality adds another layer.


A contained integration using an existing model may increase a mid-to-large project budget by roughly 10–20%, while custom models, data pipelines, real-time processing, and extensive evaluation can push the premium toward 20–40% or more.


Usage-based model fees also continue after launch.


## **How Your Build Path Changes the Price**


Who builds the application often affects the web app development cost more than any individual feature. Each path trades upfront cost against speed, control, technical responsibility, and production readiness.


**Build path** **Typical cost** **Best for** **Main limitation**


Custom agency $80,000–$300,000+ Funded, complex products Highest upfront cost


Freelancers $10,000–$100,000+ Defined scopes and smaller budgets Coordination and continuity risk


No-code platform $0–$549+ per month Non-technical MVPs Customization and platform limits


AI app builder $0–$100+ per month before usage Fast validation and early launches Output quality and flexibility vary


Self-built with AI and a framework Tooling and hosting costs Technical founders Founder owns maintenance


**Custom agencies:** Handle strategy, design, development, testing, and launch. Business-ready apps often cost $80,000–$150,000+, while complex platforms can exceed $200,000.


**Freelancers:** Lower the upfront cost, especially with a clear scope, but founders may need to coordinate design, frontend, backend, and QA separately.


**No-code platforms:** Replace custom development and infrastructure with a subscription. Costs can start free but rise with higher plans and usage.


**AI app builders:** Generate much of the application from natural-language instructions. They can produce MVPs far more cheaply than a hired team, although quality, flexibility, and production readiness vary.


**Self-built with AI and a framework:** Keeps tooling costs low but shifts code review, security, deployment, monitoring, and maintenance to the founder.


A mid-complexity custom build may require $80,000–$180,000 and several months.


An AI-built MVP may begin at under $100 per month and reach users in days or weeks, but the two outputs provide different levels of polish, testing, support, and assurance.


AI and no-code are strongest for validating demand; custom development becomes more valuable as requirements, scale, and risk increase.


### **What No-Code and AI Builders Can Save You**


No-code and AI tools save money by removing two expensive steps: translating designs into working code and manually connecting common infrastructure such as databases, authentication, hosting, and deployment.


The savings are real because less custom work is being performed.


The tradeoff is that the skipped work may also reduce control, portability, or flexibility. Builders should therefore check code ownership, export options, usage-based pricing, and platform limits before committing to a long-term product.


## **Developer and Agency Rates by Region**


Most custom-development quotes are estimated hours multiplied by an hourly rate. Typical rates fall into these broad ranges:


**Region** **Typical hourly rate**


North America / Western Europe $60–$180+


Latin America $35–$75


Eastern Europe $30–$75


Asia Pacific $20–$55


North America and Western Europe usually sit at the top of the range.


Latin America offers closer time-zone overlap for US clients, while Eastern Europe and Asia Pacific are generally more affordable. Senior developers and specialists in AI, security, or cloud infrastructure may charge above these ranges.


Freelancers often cost less than agencies because their rates do not include project management, account support, and other overhead.


However, founders may need to coordinate design, frontend, backend, and QA themselves.


A lower hourly rate does not always mean a lower total bill. Communication delays, rework, unclear requirements, or limited experience can increase the hours needed to deliver the same result.


## **Hosting and Server Costs**


A pre-revenue web app can often be hosted for $0–$100 per month. Costs rise when the app needs a separate database, load balancing, backups, additional environments, or sustained traffic.


**Setup** **Typical monthly cost**


Serverless, low traffic $0–$20


Fixed-price starter server $5–$12


Small app, single instance $20–$60


Small production app with database and load balancer $40–$200


High-traffic or redundant application $500–$5,000+


- **Serverless hosting:** Charges by request and execution time, so low-traffic apps may remain within free tiers. It works well for early products with unpredictable usage.
- **Fixed-price servers:** Run continuously and cost the same whether the app is busy or idle. Starter plans can begin around $5 per month.


A production setup may also need a managed database, load balancer, backups, and separate testing environments. These additions can push a small app into the $40–$200 monthly range.


Most founders do not need expensive infrastructure at launch. Hosting becomes a major cost only when traffic, data volume, uptime requirements, or architectural complexity increase.


## **Third-Party Services: The Costs That Don’t Show Up in a Quote**


A development quote rarely includes every service needed to run the app after launch. Payments, authentication, email, storage, maps, and analytics create recurring costs that grow with usage.


**Service** **Function** **Current pricing**


Stripe Payments 2.9% + $0.30 per domestic card transaction


Auth0 Authentication Free tier; Essentials starts at $35/month


SendGrid Transactional email Free tier; Essentials from $19.95/month


SendGrid Pro Email with dedicated Internet Protocol (IP) address From $89.95/month


Cloud storage / content delivery network (CDN) Files and media Usage-based; Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) Standard starts at $0.023 per GB-month


Key cost points:


- Processing $10,000 across 100 Stripe transactions would cost about $320.
- Auth0’s free plan covers early usage, while paid tiers add higher limits and production features.
- SendGrid offers a small free allowance, with paid plans starting around $20 per month.
- Storage may be inexpensive at first, but requests, retrieval, and bandwidth also affect the bill.


Vendor pricing can also change. Google Maps Platform, for example, replaced its recurring $200 monthly credit with service-specific free usage caps in 2025.


Budget for price increases and avoid dependencies that would be difficult to replace.


## **Maintenance Costs After Launch**


Launching the application does not end the development bill. A common benchmark is to reserve 15–25% of the original build cost each year for maintenance.


That means budgeting roughly:


- $7,500–$12,500 annually for a $50,000 app
- $15,000–$25,000 annually for a $100,000 app
- $37,500–$62,500 annually for a $250,000 app


Maintenance usually covers:


- Security patches and dependency updates
- Bug fixes and compatibility work
- Monitoring and performance improvements
- Small changes based on user feedback


Costs tend to be lower for focused apps with clean code and few integrations. They rise for older systems, regulated products, real-time features, or apps that depend heavily on external APIs.


Major new features should be budgeted separately. Maintenance keeps the existing product secure and reliable; it does not cover a major redesign or product expansion.


## **How Can You Reduce the Cost of Your Web App?**


The biggest savings come from reducing unnecessary scope and avoiding infrastructure work that does not differentiate the product.


- **Start with a focused MVP:** Build only the core workflow needed to test demand. Extra roles, integrations, reports, and automations can wait until users prove they need them.
- **Validate before hiring a full team:** No-code or AI app builders can turn an idea into a working prototype before you commit tens of thousands of dollars to custom development.
- **Use a platform with infrastructure included:** Bundled authentication, databases, hosting, deployment, and monitoring reduce both integration work and recurring service costs.
- **Choose widely supported technology:** Popular frameworks are easier to hire for, maintain, and extend than niche stacks that require expensive specialists.
- **Keep ownership of the code:** Exportable code gives you the option to change hosting, hire developers, or move to another platform without rebuilding from zero.
- **Write clear requirements early:** Defined user roles, workflows, data, and edge cases reduce rework and prevent scope from expanding during development.


The cheapest first build is not always the cheapest long-term option. Compare migration limits, usage charges, maintenance needs, and code ownership before choosing a platform.


## **The Bootstrapped Path vs. the Funded Path**


Consider the same product idea: a small SaaS application with user accounts, a dashboard, stored data, and Stripe payments.


### **Bootstrapped Founder Using an AI App Builder**


**Cost** **Year-one estimate**


Modelence Starter plan $240


Cloud environment About $108–$264


Authentication and database Included


Monitoring and deployment Included


Stripe processing 2.9% + $0.30 per domestic card transaction


**Fixed year-one total** **About $348–$504, plus payment fees**


Modelence Starter costs $20 per month, while its Micro and Small cloud environments are estimated at about $9 and $22 per month. App Builder usage beyond the included allowance and heavier infrastructure would increase the total.


### **Funded Startup Hiring an Agency**


**Cost** **Year-one estimate**


Agency design and development $150,000


Hosting $2,400


Third-party services $1,200


Maintenance at 15% of build cost $22,500


**Year-one total** **$176,100**


This example assumes a mid-complexity custom build, $200 per month in hosting, $100 per month in external services, and a full annual maintenance reserve.


The bootstrapped path is dramatically cheaper, but it does not automatically provide the same design process, testing depth, technical review, or ongoing support as an agency. It works best for validating demand and reaching early users.


The funded path makes more sense when the requirements are already proven and reliability, compliance, integrations, or professional delivery justify the investment.

## Frequently asked questions (FAQs)


How much does it cost to build a web app from scratch?


A professionally built web app typically costs $20,000–$50,000 for a focused MVP, $80,000–$150,000+ for a business-ready product, and $200,000–$400,000+ for an enterprise platform.


How much does it cost to build a web application versus a simple website?


A simple professionally designed website may cost $1,000–$5,000, while a custom web app usually starts around $20,000 because it requires backend logic, databases, accounts, and integrations.


Can I build a web app for free?


You can prototype one using free plans and open-source tools, but launching usually introduces costs for hosting, domains, infrastructure, or additional usage.


How much does it cost to host a web app per month?


A low-traffic app may cost $0–$100 per month, while production systems with databases, redundancy, and sustained usage can cost hundreds or thousands.


How long does it take to build a web app?


Traditional development can take several months, while no-code and AI tools may produce an initial MVP in days or weeks, depending on complexity.


Is it cheaper to use an AI app builder or hire developers?


An AI builder is usually much cheaper for prototyping and early validation, while developers remain more suitable for highly specialized, regulated, or technically complex applications.


What ongoing costs should I budget for after launch?


Plan for hosting, payment processing, email, storage, monitoring, security updates, bug fixes, and future product improvements.
